name: Virto Commerce
title: Virto Commerce SvelteKit Storefront — Svelte Commerce
description: Svelte Commerce on Virto Commerce’s GraphQL API: 28 of 43 services wired, with cart, checkout and sign-in, no gaps recorded. Setup, environment and fixes.
lede: Targeting Virto Commerce meant choosing which of its API generations to wire against; the connector speaks its GraphQL API. Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired, and CONNECTORS.md records no gaps.
verdict: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired, and no gaps are recorded. Orders are placed through the payment methods the Virto store itself exposes; a gateway the store has not configured is refused with a message saying so.

quickStart.text: one connector at a time: remove the two the storefront ships with, add this one
point it at your Virto Commerce platform

env.name: PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_API_URL
env.note: Base URL of your Virto Commerce platform. Boot fails, naming this variable, if it is missing.

env.name: PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_STORE_ID
env.note: The Virto store the storefront serves.

env.name: PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_CULTURE_NAME
env.note: Such as `en-US`. Passed on nearly every catalogue, cart and order query; read once from the store if unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_CURRENCY_CODE
env.note: Such as `USD`. Passed on every priced query; read once from the store if unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_CATALOG_ID
env.note: Needed to filter products by category; read once from the store if unset.

env.name: PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_ACCESS_TOKEN
env.note: An access token to start from, sent in the `Authorization` header.

env.name: PUBLIC_CONNECTOR
env.note: Only when more than one connector is installed: `@misiki/virto-connector` names the one this build runs on.

envNote: `init.ts` hands the connector every `PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_*` variable that is set, camel-cased — the prefix follows the product, not the package, which is `virto-connector`. The guide also lists `PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_API_KEY`, `PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_API_SECRET`, `PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_ACCESS_KEY` and `PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_CHANNEL_ID`; the connector’s source does not read them.
backendSettings: Configure the payment methods you want shoppers to use on the Virto store itself: the connector places orders through `cart.availablePaymentMethods`, and refuses a gateway the store does not offer.
howItWorks: The connector speaks Virto Commerce’s GraphQL API, which wants culture, currency and catalogue as explicit arguments on most operations. Whatever you leave unset is read once from the store’s own record and remembered. Checkout places the order with a payment method the store exposes, matched by name — or, for cash on delivery, by a manual payment method.
limitations: No gaps are recorded for Virto Commerce in CONNECTORS.md.

troubleshooting.problem: Boot fails with “the virto connector is active but PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_API_URL is not set”
troubleshooting.fix: Add `PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_API_URL` to `.env`. A production Node build and Docker read `PUBLIC_*` from the process environment rather than `.env`, so set it on your deploy platform too.

troubleshooting.problem: The build stops with “Several commerce connectors are installed … Set PUBLIC_CONNECTOR to pick one”
troubleshooting.fix: More than one `@misiki/*-connector` is in `package.json` and none is Litekart’s. Uninstall the ones you do not run — a fresh clone also lists `@misiki/vendure-connector` — or set `PUBLIC_CONNECTOR='@misiki/virto-connector'`.

troubleshooting.problem: `[virto] no native implementation for get /api/...` in the console
troubleshooting.fix: The connector’s REST guard caught a path inherited from Litekart and answered it empty instead of requesting it. Each path is reported once. Harmless if Virto Commerce has no such feature; if it has one, the fix belongs in the connector’s matching service.

faq.q: Can I run a Virto Commerce store on Svelte Commerce today?
faq.a: Cart, checkout and sign-in are wired against Virto’s GraphQL API and no gaps are recorded. Orders go through the payment methods your Virto store exposes. Like every connector, it has not been run against a live production Virto store.

faq.q: How do I switch Svelte Commerce to Virto Commerce?
faq.a: Remove the connectors the storefront ships with, install `@misiki/virto-connector`, set `PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_API_URL` in `.env` and start the dev server. `vite.config.ts` resolves whichever connector is installed, so no file in the storefront changes.

faq.q: Which payment methods can shoppers use on Virto Commerce?
faq.a: The ones your Virto store exposes through `cart.availablePaymentMethods`. Cash on delivery maps to a manual payment method; a gateway the store has not configured is refused with a message saying so, rather than faked.

api.surface: The connector calls Virto Commerce’s xAPI, a GraphQL schema served at `POST <PUBLIC_VIRTO_COMMERCE_API_URL>/graphql`, and leaves the `/api/...` REST controllers alone because they are the back-office API and need platform permissions a shopper token never holds.
api.auth: A shopper signs in through OpenIddict at `POST /connect/token`, form-encoded, with `grant_type=password`, `scope=offline_access` and the `storeId`; the connector sends the access token back as `Authorization: <token_type> <access_token>` and, on a 401, tries the `refresh_token` grant once before giving up.

calls.what: `products` with `storeId`, `userId`, `cultureName`, `currencyCode`, `filter`, `query`, `sort`, `first` and `after`; a product page runs `slugInfo(permalink:)` and then `product(id:)`
`categories` with `storeId`, `filter`, `query`, `sort`, `first` and `after`, and `products` with the filter `category.subtree:{catalogId}/{categoryId}` for a category’s products
`products` with Virto’s `filter` grammar (quoted property values, `price.usd:[100 TO 200)`, `category.subtree:`) plus `facet`
the `cart` query, and the `addItem`, `changeCartItemQuantity`, `removeCartItem`, `clearCart`, `addCoupon` and `removeCoupon` mutations, each taking a `command` with a non-null `userId`
`cart { availablePaymentMethods }`, then `addOrUpdateCartPayment` with the `paymentGatewayCode`, `createOrderFromCart`, `initializePayment` and, on return, `authorizePayment`
`POST /connect/token`, then `me`; registration through `requestRegistration`, resets through `sendPasswordResetEmail` and `resetPasswordByToken`

rules: GraphQL answers HTTP 200 even when an operation fails, so the connector throws on a non-empty `errors` array, and it checks the `validationErrors` that many mutations return inside `data`.
The `after` argument looks like a cursor but is a numeric offset, `(page - 1) * first`, and page totals come from `totalCount` in the response body.
Products and categories cannot be fetched by slug, so a product page costs two queries: `slugInfo(permalink:)` for the object id, then `product(id:)`.

A shopper who has not signed in is Virto’s anonymous user, carried by a cookie, so every request goes out with `credentials: 'include'`, and the platform’s CORS settings must allow credentials from the storefront’s origin or the anonymous cart is lost.
Sort arguments go out in Virto’s `field:direction` form joined by `;`, with `createdAt` sent as `createddate` and `popularity` as `priority`.
